('''MSI'''; {{zh|c=微星科技股份有限公司}}) is a Taiwanese multinational corporation based in [[New Taipei City]], Taiwan. The company designs, develops, and provides [[computer hardware]], related products, and services. Its product lineup includes laptops, desktop computers, [[motherboard]], [[graphics card|graphics card]]s, [[all-in-one computer]]s, [[server (computing)|servers]], industrial computers, peripherals, and automotive infotainment systems. MSI was founded on August 4, 1986, by Hsu Hsiang (Joseph Hsu), Huang Chin-Ching (Jeans Huang), Lin Wen-Tung (Frank Lin), Yu Hsien-Neng (Kenny Yu), and Lu Chi-Lung (Henry Lu). It is listed on the [[Taiwan Stock Exchange]].{{cite web |author= |title=Micro-Star International Co (2377:Taiwan Stock Exchange) |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/research/stocks/snapshot/snapshot.asp?ticker=2377:TT |access-date=5 February 2015 |website=[[Bloomberg News]]}}{{Cite web |title=Micro-Star International Co Ltd |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/profile/company/2377:TT |website=[[Bloomberg L.P.|Bloomberg]]}} ==Operations== First starting its business in [[New Taipei City]], Taiwan, MSI later expanded into China, setting up its [[Bao'an District|Bao'an]] plant in [[Shenzhen]] in 2000 and establishing [[research and development]] facilities in [[Kunshan]] in 2001. It also provides global warranty services in North America, Central/South America, Asia, Australia and Europe. MSI's offices in [[Zhonghe District]], New Taipei City, Taiwan, serve as the company's headquarters, and house a number of different divisions and services.{{cite web|author=|title=headquarters|url= http://www.msi.com/about/contact-us|access-date=21 October 2015}} Manufacturing initially took place at plants in Taiwan, but has been moved elsewhere. Many MSI graphics cards are manufactured at its plant in mainland China. The company has branch offices in the Americas, Europe, Asia, Australia and South Africa. As of 2015, the company has a global presence in over 120 countries. MSI and Syrma SGS announced their collaboration to make laptops in [[Chennai]] on January 10, 2025. MSI will [[transfer technology]] to Syrma SGS for localized production in [[India]].{{Cite web |last=Ghosh |first=Anupama |date=2025-01-10 |title=MSI partners with Syrma SGS for laptop manufacturing in India |url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/markets/stock-markets/msi-partners-with-syrma-sgs-for-laptop-manufacturing-in-india/article69084355.ece |access-date=2025-01-11 |website=BusinessLine |language=en}}{{Cite news |date=2025-01-10 |title=MSI joins hands with Syrma SGS to manufacture laptops for Indian market |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tech/technology/msi-joins-hands-with-syrma-sgs-to-manufacture-laptops-for-indian-market/articleshow/117125370.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2025-01-11 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}} ==Products== The company first built its reputation on developing and manufacturing [[motherboard]]s for [[computers]], and graphics cards. It established its subsidiary [[FUNTORO]] in 2008 for the vehicle [[infotainment]] market. It provides many computer and tech oriented products including [[laptop]]s, [[desktop computer|desktops]], [[Computer monitor|monitor]]s, motherboards, graphics cards, power supply units, computer cases and liquid cooler for gamers and content creators, all-in-one PCs, mobile workstations, servers, IPCs, multimedia peripherals, vehicle infotainment, and an autonomous mobility robot.{{cite web|url=https://www.digitimes.com/news/a20191014PD206.html/|title=MSI unveils AMR for robot market|author=|date=14 October 2019 |access-date=4 December 2019}} When established in 1986, MSI focused on the design and manufacturing of motherboards and add-on cards. Later that year, it introduced the first over-clockable [[Intel 80286|286]] motherboard. In 1989, MSI introduced its first [[Intel 80486|486]] motherboard; in 1990, its first [[Socket 7]] based motherboard; in 1993, its first 586 motherboard; and in 1995, its Dual Pentium Pro-based motherboard. In 1997, it introduced its Intel [[Pentium II]]-based motherboard with Intel MMX Technology, along with its first graphics card product and first barebone product. In 2002, it released its first PC2PC Bluetooth & WLAN motherboard.{{citation needed|date=April 2020}} In 2000, MSI introduced its first [[set-top box]] product (MS-5205);{{cite web|url=https://www.msi.com/news/detail/ehPgj2TfzcbuFhNJF0mAGSwPGZfwY7sGBWT6igKINlGQ6F_otqCMOFnpm4Ad99_h0SlM78WxSrlmPWBWtvwTAg~~|title=Micro-Star International Announces MS-5205 Set-Top Box|author=|access-date=5 February 2015|archive-date=11 August 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200811165443/https://www.msi.com/news/detail/ehPgj2TfzcbuFhNJF0mAGSwPGZfwY7sGBWT6igKINlGQ6F_otqCMOFnpm4Ad99_h0SlM78WxSrlmPWBWtvwTAg~~|url-status=dead}} in 2003, its first Pen Tablet PC product (PenNote3100);{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=T9I6-TOH-po|title=MSI PenNote 3100 Tablet PC|author=|website=[[YouTube]]|date=18 August 2008 |access-date=5 February 2015}} and in 2004, its first Notebook product (M510C).{{cite web|url=http://www.hardwarezone.com/articles/view.php?id=1226|title=MSI Megabook M510C|author=|access-date=5 February 2015}} In 2009, MSI introduced its first Ultra Slim Notebook (X320),{{cite web|url=http://www.msi.com/product/nb/X320X300.html#hero-overview|title=MSI X320 Ultra Slim Notebook|author=|access-date=5 February 2015|archive-date=24 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150624035615/http://www.msi.com/product/nb/X320X300.html#hero-overview|url-status=dead}} and first all-in-one PC (AP1900).{{cite web|url=http://www.msi.com/product/aio/Wind_Top_AP1900.html#hero-overview|title=MSI AP1900 All-in-One PC|author=|access-date=5 February 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150716130303/http://www.msi.com/product/aio/Wind_Top_AP1900.html#hero-overview|archive-date=16 July 2015|url-status=dead}} MSI released their first [[digital audio player]] in 2003, in a line named MEGA.{{Cite web|url=https://www.msi.com/news/detail/MSIMP3PlayershavewonJapansprestigious347|title=MSI Global - the Leading Brand in High-end Gaming & Professional Creation}} In 2008, MSI sponsored [[Fnatic]] and dived into the PC gaming market. Its GAMING series features laptops, desktops, [[motherboard]]s, graphic cards, all-in-one PCs, and gaming [[peripheral]]s designed for gamers and power users. New designs of its GS65 Stealth Thin and GE63 Raider RGB laptops earned the company an 84 out of 100 and put it on the top spot.{{cite web |author= |date=14 August 2018 |title=Best & Worst Gaming Laptop Brands 2018 |url=https://www.laptopmag.com/articles/gaming-laptop-brand-ratings |access-date=August 29, 2018}} On 7 October 2020, MSI released a public statement about their subsidiary Starlit scalping MSI-made [[GeForce RTX 30 series|Nvidia GeForce RTX 3080 and 3090]] [[graphics processing unit]]s (GPUs), and selling them for higher than MSRP on [[eBay]].{{Cite web |last=Kan |first=Michale |date=7 October 2020 |title=MSI Subsidiary Caught Scalping RTX 3080, 3090 Cards on eBay. |url=https://sea.pcmag.com/graphics-cards/39516/msi-subsidiary-caught-scalping-rtx-3080-3090-cards-on-ebay |access-date=2021-07-25 |website=pcmag.com |language=en-us}} During the [[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]], MSI refused to withdraw from the Russian market. Research by [[Jeffrey Sonnenfeld]] of Yale University put MSI in the [[Yale CELI List of Companies]] category of "Digging In - Defying Demands for Exit or Reduction of Activities", the only Taiwanese company in the database.{{cite web|author= |title= Over 750 Companies Have Curtailed Operations in Russia—But Some Remain |website= [[Yale School of Management]] |url=https://som.yale.edu/story/2022/over-750-companies-have-curtailed-operations-russia-some-remain |access-date= 18 September 2022}} MSI issued a statement on March 28, 2022, claiming that it abides by all international regulations in terms of its sales and operations in Russia.{{cite web|author= |title= MSI says it abides by international rules on sales to Russia |website= OCACNEWS |url=https://ocacnews.net/article/306278/ |access-date= 16 November 2022}} At Computex 2023, MSI revealed a collaboration with Mercedes-AMG for a special edition of its Alpha 17 gaming laptop. This limited-edition model features design elements inspired by the AMG performance brand, integrating the aesthetics and luxury of Mercedes-AMG with high-performance gaming hardware. The partnership emphasizes both brands' focus on speed, precision, and cutting-edge technology.{{Cite web |url=https://www.tomshardware.com/news/msi-computex-mercedes-amg-alpha-17/ |title=MSI Gets Fast & Furious With Mercedes-AMG Gaming Laptop |date=2023-05-30 |access-date=2024-09-27 |website=MSI}} In 2024, MSI Gaming Arena hosted a Dota 2 e-sports tournament in Southeast Asia. Teams were chosen through regional qualifiers for the online playoffs, which were scheduled from September 27 to October 6.{{Cite web |url=https://mga.msi.com/en/home |title=MSI MGA 2024 |date=2024-09-05 |access-date=2024-09-20 |website=MSI}} The Discovery documentary ''Esports: The Rise of the New King'' examines the rapid transformation of gaming into a prominent sport, premiering in August 2023. It focuses on MSI's contribution to esports, particularly in hardware and cooling technology, while also showcasing events like ESL One New York and the MSI MGA finals. The program highlights the role of PC gaming in driving hardware sales and the growing partnership between manufacturers and esports tournaments.{{Cite web |url=https://www.hardwarezone.com.sg/tech-news-discovery-network-breaks-gaming-esports-rise-new-king/ |title=Discovery network breaks into gaming with Esports: The Rise of the New King |date=2019-08-05 |access-date=2024-09-27 |website=MSI}} MSI introduced new server platforms powered by [[Intel]]'s Xeon processors, featuring six performance cores for improved computational performance. These servers are designed to enhance AI, data processing, and cloud computing capabilities. The new platforms highlight MSI's focus on scalability and advanced technology for high-performance computing environments.{{Cite web |url=https://www.hpcwire.com/off-the-wire/msi-unveils-new-server-platforms-powered-by-intel-xeon-6-p-cores/ |title=MSI Unveils New Server Platforms Powered by Intel Xeon 6 P-Cores |date=2024-09-24 |access-date=2024-09-27 |website=MSI}} At the 2024 Taipei Auto Show, MSI unveiled a new range of smart electric vehicle (EV) chargers. The lineup features residential and commercial models, including the EV Life charger, which is compatible with both U.S. and European charging standards. MSI's commercial chargers offer payment options and advanced management features, such as parking management via license plate recognition. Micro-Star International Co., Ltd. (MSI; Chinese: 微星科技股份有限公司) is a Taiwanese multinational corporation based in New Taipei City, Taiwan. The company designs, develops, and provides computer hardware, related products, and services. Its product lineup includes laptops, desktop computers, motherboard, graphics cards, all-in-one computers, servers, industrial computers, peripherals, and automotive infotainment systems.
MSI was founded on August 4, 1986, by Hsu Hsiang (Joseph Hsu), Huang Chin-Ching (Jeans Huang), Lin Wen-Tung (Frank Lin), Yu Hsien-Neng (Kenny Yu), and Lu Chi-Lung (Henry Lu). It is listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange.
